title: Embeddings concurrency gating and hotkey management
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Several customers and internal load tests show pathological tail latency and request loss during high-concurrency bursts to embeddings endpoints. Root causes include small numbers of hot keys (single-tenant or multi-tenant) monopolizing worker slots, per-tenant spikes bypassing fair admission, and the autoscaler reacting too slowly to sudden QPS jumps. This ticket scopes a coordinated set of runtime controls to stabilize p99/p999 latency while preserving throughput and fairness.
goals: 1) Prevent single-hotkey request storms from causing system-wide p99/p999 regressions. 2) Provide predictable latency SLOs under bursty workloads. 3) Allow controlled overcommit for non-SLO tenants via priority lanes. 4) Reduce emergency scaling events by smoothing admission and enabling fast, local headroom adjustments.
success_metrics: p99 latency for embeddings endpoints <= 120ms under 95th-percentile burst patterns
p999 latency reduction >= 30% versus baseline bursts
<0.1% request drops due to queue overflow at 99th QPS percentile
10% reduction in autoscaler churn during observed spike traces
proposed_solution:
Design a multi-layered concurrency gating system:
- Per-worker multi-queue: separate 'priority' and 'best-effort' lanes with bounded capacity. Priority lane reserved for customer tiers and requests tagged with SLO=true. Best-effort receives throttling when backlog grows.
- Hotkey detector: lightweight sliding-window counter per key (hash-based sharding) that identifies 'hot' embedding keys and applies local rate caps and short-lived token buckets to prevent slot monopolization.
- Tenant-level circuit: per-tenant concurrency limiter that integrates with routing metadata and applies backpressure via immediate 429 when tenant limits exceeded, with exponential backoff hints returned in headers.
- Predictive short-term headroom: a local fast-provisioner that temporarily increases worker concurrency allowance based on a 1s exponential moving average of queue growth and request latency, bounded by global autoscaler policy to avoid resource blowouts.
- Admission controller API: central config with fine-grained rules (per-tenant caps, priority lists, hotkey thresholds) surfaced to Console for experiments. All decisions are logged for replay and debugging.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- More complex runtime increases risk of bugs; will incrementally roll out with feature flags.
- Local short-term headroom may mask actual capacity shortages and delay autoscaler response; mitigation: tight global bounds and autoscaler backstop.
- Additional per-request checks add CPU overhead; optimize hotkey detector with probabilistic counters and sampling.
- Tenants may see more 429s; we'll provide SDK guidance and retry headers for graceful degradation.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): implement hotkey detector + per-worker queues behind feature flag; run against replayed production traces and synthetic hotkey storms.
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5% of hosts handling non-critical traffic and monitor SLOs and CPU overhead.
Phase 3 (gradual): expand to 25% -> 50% -> 100% while enabling tenant-level caps for a small set of pilot customers; collect feedback from Solutions Eng.
Phase 4 (defaults): expose basic controls in Console and default sensible thresholds for hosted customers. Rollback: feature flag off reverts to previous behavior instantly.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add metrics: hotkey_count_by_shard, per_worker_queue_length_{priority,besteffort}, tenant_concurrency_in_use, headroom_adjustments, admission_429_rate. Create SLO dashboards (p50/p90/p99/p999) and an on-call runbook for elevated 429 or queue-exhaustion alerts. Instrument structured logs for first 1M gated decisions for postmortem analysis.
implementation_notes: Runtime changes touch: request router (admission hooks), worker loop (multi-queue dequeue), metrics exporter, and autoscaler policy. Use feature flag 'embeddings_concurrency_v2'. Start with deterministic tests and end-to-end harness using synthetic shards from perf infra.
